title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 98-100). Grothendieck is working on a point-free notion of 'space'. A space is a complete lattice Σ, possibly carrying two extra structures:
- a complementation-type operation C;
- a 'disjunction structure', i.e. a disjointness relation a ⊥ b, written in the manuscript with a symbol like |o|.

Correspondences Σ → Σ' are maps commuting with arbitrary Sups. The previous page shows two things. First, Corr(Σ,Σ') is a complete lattice under the pointwise order. Second, for the 'trivial' (discrete) case Σ_E = P(E), there is an isomorphism Corr(Σ_E, Σ') ≅ Σ'^E: a sup-map out of a powerset is determined by its values on singletons. In that discrete case the structures C and ⊥ can be transported 'term by term': (Cf)(x) = C(f(x)), and f ⊥ g iff f(x) ⊥ g(x) for every x ∈ E. The first line of this page is that pointwise definition of the disjointness relation; the image shows the |o| symbol, not ≤.

Observation on this page. The pointwise definitions do not survive when f is applied to arbitrary subsets A ∈ P(E) rather than to points.
- Complement: (Cf)(A) = Sup_{x∈A} C f(x), whereas C(f(A)) = C(Sup_{x∈A} f(x)) = Inf_{x∈A} C f(x) (De Morgan, for an honest complement). These differ in general.
- Disjointness: f ⊥ g does not imply f(A) ⊥ g(A), because f(x) need not be disjoint from g(y) when x ≠ y.

Conclusion drawn. Defining C or ⊥ on Corr(Σ,Σ') for general Σ seems tied to the existence of 'points'. Candidates are the minimal elements (atoms) of Σ \ {0_Σ}, or some other objects that could stand in for points. This is exactly the point-free versus pointed tension of locale theory.

New question (continued on p.100). In the set-theoretic presentation, a correspondence is a graph Γ ⊂ E × E'. It factors as Γ = f' ∘ ᵗf, i.e. a span: an inverse image A ↦ f⁻¹(A) followed by a direct image B ↦ f'(B). The two kinds of maps are characterized as follows:
- comorphisms ᵗf are the correspondences commuting with C;
- morphisms f' are those whose transpose commutes with C.
Grothendieck asks whether such a comorphism/morphism factorization exists for general 'disjunctive/spatial maps'.
errors: No genuine error once the relation symbol is read correctly as disjointness (|o|) rather than ≤. If it were the pointwise order ≤, the claim 'f ≤ g does not imply f(A) ≤ g(A)' would be false: sup-maps are monotone and f(A) = Sup_{x∈A} f(x), so f ≤ g pointwise does give f(A) ≤ g(A). The machine transcription's ≤ therefore misrepresents the content.
Minor: the identification of 'points' with minimal elements of Σ \ {0} only works for atomic lattices; Grothendieck himself flags that other objects may be needed.

ideas.what: Correspondences as Sup-preserving maps between complete lattices; Corr(P(E), Σ') ≅ Σ'^E
ideas.modern_name: Category Sup of sup-lattices; free sup-lattice P(E) on a set E; relations as Kleisli maps of the powerset monad
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical lattice theory; Joyal–Tierney (1984) for the Sup viewpoint in locale theory

ideas.what: Pointwise structures (complement, disjointness) on Σ'^E do not extend to evaluations on subsets: (Cf)(A) ≠ C(f(A)), f ⊥ g does not imply f(A) ⊥ g(A)
ideas.modern_name: De Morgan failure / sup-maps do not preserve complements or orthogonality

ideas.what: Need for 'points' (atoms or substitutes) in order to define complement/orthogonality on hom-objects between point-free spaces
ideas.modern_name: Points of locales; atomic vs. pointless lattices; orthogonality spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone (locales); Foulis–Randall, Dacey (orthogonality spaces)

ideas.what: Factorization of a relation Γ ⊂ E × E' as direct image after inverse image (span), with inverse images characterized by commuting with complement
ideas.modern_name: Span/tabulation of relations in a regular category; Set^op ≃ CABA (Tarski/Lindenbaum duality); Beck–Chevalley/allegory tabulations

missed.claim: The open question of whether general 'disjunctive/spatial' correspondences (sup-maps between complete lattices with complement/orthogonality) admit a comorphism-then-morphism factorization, as relations do. This would be a tabulation theorem for a point-free category of relations with orthogonality.
missed.quote: Une question non dénuée d'intérêt [?] est la suivante ... Γ ⊂ E×E' des correspondances
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to tabulations in allegories/quantaloid-enriched categories and to orthogonality/Chu-space frameworks, but the specific question for lattices with disjointness is a minor variant of known material. It is of modest interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: These are personal foundational notes on point-free 'spaces' with complement/disjunction structure. The observations are elementary and correct, and the factorization question is closely related to known theory (allegories, CABA duality, locales). It is biographically interesting that Grothendieck explored point-free lattices with orthogonality in 1986, but there is no hidden result here.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the relation symbol is a disjointness symbol (looks like |o|), not ≤: 'f |o| g ⟺ ∀x∈E, f(x) |o| g(x)', and later 'f |o| g ⇏ f(A) |o| g(A)'.
'Conv(Σ,Σ')' should read 'Corr(Σ,Σ')' (correspondences), consistent with the neighbouring pages.
'on n'a même [?] [-plus-] {+en général+}': 'plus' is struck and 'en général' is added above it; read roughly 'on n'a même plus en général'.
The margin note reads 'A ∈ [crossed symbol]_E = 𝔓(E)', likely 'Σ_E = 𝔓(E)'.
'définir C ou ≤' should be 'définir C ou |o|' (the disjunction relation).
'd'autres objets arithmétiques [?]' is uncertain; the word may be 'mathématiques' or similar.
Last line: 'les graphes Γ ⊂ E×E' des correspondances', followed by a struck 'celles-ci peut'.
